messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: PD#4281 — inference-queue-backlog HIGH. Affected service: inference-cell-eu-west-1. Symptom: sustained queue depth > 60k, 95th p95 gen latency > 12s. Auto-escalation in 2m if unacked.
pagerduty-bot: @lucy (oncall) — page delivered, respond to acknowledge.
lucy (oncall): Acked. Looking now. Any customer reports? :eyes:
samir (customer-success): We're seeing spikes in support tickets from two enterprise customers — some 503s and long tail latency from API calls since ~09:02 UTC. Sending sample request ids.
jordan (sre): Can someone dump autoscaler logs and HPA status? If HPA can't spin nodes, we might be rate-limited or hitting cloud quota.
maya (runtime): Adding telemetry: queue_length: 62,412; backpressure_ratio: 0.78; cold_kv_cache_misses up 4x. Batching increased but worker pods stuck at 12/PodMax.
alex (infra): I'm seeing k8s: api-server returning 429s for scale requests. From controller-manager logs: \n```\nE0323 09:03:12.123456 1 event.go:291] Could not update HPA status: the server is currently unable to handle the request (get horizontalpodautoscalers.autoscaling/v2)\nW0323 09:03:13.789123 1 scale_controller.go:201] scale request rejected: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = nodepool quota exceeded\n```\nLooks like we hit shared nodepool quota; new nodes are being throttled by cloud provider.
lucy (oncall): So autoscaler attempted scale but provider quota blocked it. Can we fallback to lower-quality model variant to reduce CPU per request? Maya?
maya (runtime): Yes — we have smaller quantized variant model-q1 compatible with current hooks. We can change routing policy to degrade to model-q1 for non-enterprise tiers. Command to flip routing policy (dry-run first):\n```\n# dry-run\nredwoodctl routing plan --from inference-v2 --to model-q1 --filter tier!=enterprise\n# apply\nredwoodctl routing apply --plan <plan-id>\n```\nThat should reduce per-token CPU by ~40%. But queue will still need some drain time.
jordan (sre): I'll attempt manual nodepool increase as emergency bypass while infra escalates quota. Alex — can you request immediate quota bump? If not, manual scale of dedicated pool for inference-cell-eu-west-1.
alex (infra): Requesting quota bump with cloud console now, marking as emergency. If provider doesn't approve in ~10m, I'll spin a temporary burst nodepool from a different region and cordon traffic via routing rule.
samir (customer-success): Can we prioritize enterprise traffic to avoid P1 customer impact?
lucy (oncall): Yes — Maya, add prioritized routing for enterprise keys to keep them on golden pool, then degrade public traffic.
maya (runtime): Doing prioritized routing now. Patch: \n```\nredwoodctl routing update --cell inference-eu-west-1 --priority-key enterprise --pin pool:golden\n```\nApplied. Enterprise requests should be pinned to fewer but healthy pods. Monitor logs for errors.
jordan (sre): Also noticed Kube API 429s might be from our control-plane autoscaler hitting provider rate-limits. Throttling window suggests backoff not aggressive. I'll temporarily increase controller-manager backoff to reduce failed attempts.
alex (infra): I've opened cloud support ticket CS-9987 (priority: urgent) requesting node quota for n2-standard burst. ETA tentative 7-15m. Spinning temporary cross-region pool as fallback now.
lucy (oncall): Good. Real-time checklist: 1) Acked PD (done), 2) Prioritize enterprise traffic (done), 3) Switch non-enterprise to model-q1 (maya in progress), 4) Request quota (alex in progress), 5) Manual node spin (jordan/alex). Keep updates every 3–5 minutes.
(2m later)
maya (runtime): model-q1 routing applied for non-enterprise. Expect CPU drop; queue processing rate should increase ~30% after current batch drain.
jordan (sre): Manual node spin-up started: +8 burst nodes added to temporary pool, kube nodes registering. Kube events show nodes Ready at 09:09 UTC. Scaling pods to match.
alex (infra): Cloud support responded — provisional quota granted +10 nodes immediate. Keeping ticket open.
samir (customer-success): Tickets update: enterprise customers report reduced errors, non-enterprise reports slowly recovering. Thanks team.
lucy (oncall): Monitor metrics. If queue depth < 5k and p95 < 2s, we'll de-escalate PD.
(7m later)
maya (runtime): metrics: queue_length=3,900; p95_gen=1.6s; success_rate 99.1%. Backpressure_ratio=0.12. Good signs.
jordan (sre): Confirm controller-manager backoff tweak prevented further 429 spam. We'll revert to normal tuning after cleanup. Leaving ops runbook note.
lucy (oncall): Closing PD? I'll leave PD acknowledged and update incident ticket with mitigation steps, root cause hypothesis: provider nodepool quota exhaustion + aggressive autoscaler retries. Action items:
- infra: pursue long-term node-quota guardrails and burst pools (alex)
- runtime: add automatic fallback to quantized model for non-enterprise when queue pressure detected (maya)
- sre: add better backoff on scale retries and alert on API 429 spike (jordan)
- cs: follow up with affected customers and provide postmortem (samir)
Will hand off to overnight on-call if needed. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
pagerduty-bot: PD#4281 status: acknowledged by lucy (oncall). Incident resolved for now; reopen if queue re-spikes.
lucy (oncall): Filing incident summary and creating follow-up tickets. Posting final metrics snapshot and linking to postmortem doc.
